page: Hetzner Cloud cx23 is an entry-level virtual server belonging to the cx family, running on the QEMU hypervisor. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores on an Intel Xeon x86_64 processor clocked at 2.0 GHz. The CPU allocation is shared, meaning compute resources are split among multiple tenants. The server is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing approximately 1.95 GB per core, and includes 40 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. It does not feature a dedicated GPU.

Performance benchmarks place the cx23 in the lower tiers of cloud compute instances. In stress-ng and Geekbench testing, both single-core and multi-core CPU performance fall within the bottom 10% of tested servers. Memory bandwidth is similarly constrained, with read-only large block transfers measuring 20.91 GB/sec and write operations at 16.93 GB/sec. Cryptographic and compression tasks, such as gzip and bzip3 operations, also register in the bottom 10%. However, the local NVMe SSD storage provides basic fast-access storage, and the system can handle lightweight Redis SET operations at 2.52 million operations per second.

The primary tradeoff of the cx23 is its shared CPU architecture, which introduces the potential for resource contention and limits sustained high-performance workloads. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server is positioned as a highly economical option for low-demand environments where resource density is prioritized over raw speed. It is best suited for lightweight workloads such as basic static web serving, development environments, small utility scripts, or low-traffic database testing.
